frequency_question: How often does comprehensive permitting or infrastructure reform successfully pass under divided government within a given two-year congressional term?
membership_rule: Includes major omnibus energy, infrastructure, or regulatory reform packages passed by both chambers and signed into law during 114th, 111th, 109th, 108th, 105th, 104th Congresses where control was divided; excludes minor single-agency tweaks or failed bills.

cases.name: 104th Congress (1995-1996): Telecommunications Act / Major Regulatory Reform attempts
111th Congress (2009-2010): American Recovery and Reinvestment Act infrastructure provisions
114th Congress (2015-2016): FAST Act (Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act)
117th Congress (2021-2022): Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
118th Congress (2023-2024): Fiscal Responsibility Act permitting provisions

provenance_note: claimed 5 hits but 6 of 6 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major bipartisan infrastructure/regulatory packages under divided/narrow control; 5 included substantive permitting or approval streamlining provisions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor rider attachments in annual appropriations bills.
validity_reason: Legislative polarization trends and omnibus vehicle reliance remain stable structural features of the US Congress across multiple cycles.
